newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks inch ahead, seen shackled.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks inch ahead, seen shackled.

text.p: Austrian shares ended ahead on Thursday after trading within a claustrophobic range and on low turnover.
Traders said the low liquidity in the market, however, did not raise hopes of the ATX index breaking out of its tight 1,020 to 1,040-point trading range.
"And there's hardly anything from the customer side," said one trader.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips added on 3.03 points, or 0.29 percent, to 1,033.26 with 10 shares gaining, nine falling and two unchanged by the close.
Traders said the only significant turnover today was in Verbund and VA Stahl. "There's one buyer for VA Stahl in the market," said one, adding that system trading boosted turnover in Verbund.
"Verbund won't go down very far -- there's always money lying below the market," said another trader. Verbund lost 2.8 schillings to 735.5 on turnover of 51,183 lots.
The day's top gainer was chip maker AMS, up 4.03 percent at 697 schillings, while the leading decliner was Lenzing, down 2.52 percent at 658.
Volume in Creditanstalt shares was meagre ahead of the deadline tomorrow for the Austrian-Italian-German consortium to present its bid for the government's stake in the bank.
Creditanstalt's preferred shares ended flat at 484 on turnover of 9,620 lots.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index up 0.14 percent at 403.84.
The September ATX future gained 7.1 points to 1,033.1 on turnover of 19,838 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 254
